mainTopic: Every attempted fix for a תודה mixed up with its תמורה is rejected; then a new משנה on paying for a vowed תודה from חולין.
overview: The background case: a תודה (thanks offering) got mixed up with its תמורה (an animal someone tried to swap into its holiness), and then one of the two died. We don't know if the animal that is left is the real תודה, which needs forty loaves, or the תמורה, which comes without bread. The ruling of רבי חייא is that there is no fix, and the גמרא now tests one possible fix after another. A backup animal fails because you don't set aside a 'leftover' on purpose. רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא's plan fails because it could create a תמורה, which is punished with lashes. Bread kept outside the courtyard wall fails because four loaves must be waved inside the עזרה, and possibly-ordinary bread may not go in. רב שישא's eighty loaves fail because some holy bread would go uneaten. רב אשי's pregnant-animal plan fails because רבי יוחנן's rule may not let the owner steer the baby. רב דימי's three-animal plan fails because it needs a new vow, and the פסוק says it is better not to vow. So there is no fix. Then a new משנה begins: someone who says 'הרי עלי תודה' must bring the animal and its loaves from חולין.

steps.title: You don't set aside an animal as a leftover from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the owner can't just bring another animal as a backup: no one sets aside an animal from the start to be a 'leftover'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does anyone set aside an animal from the very beginning to be a leftover?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the reason why bringing another animal does not fix the mixed-up תודה case. A planned 'leftover' animal is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner brings a new animal and the one already standing turns out to be the real תודה, the new animal would just be an extra, a 'leftover'. Leftovers can happen by accident, but you may not set one aside on purpose. So this fix is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: set aside / designate an animal for a קרבן
from the start, on purpose (לכתחילה)
leftovers: extra animals that turned out not to be needed

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question. It explains the earlier ruling that the case has 'no fix', by knocking down one possible fix.

phrases.english: And does one set aside, from the start, for leftovers?
phrases.notes: He means: you can't plan from the beginning for an animal to end up as an unneeded extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, giving the reason one suggested fix fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the fix of bringing a backup animal for the mixed-up תודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plan means setting aside an animal on purpose to be a leftover, which is not done.

steps.title: A new fix: bring an animal and bread with a double condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא suggests bringing a new animal plus bread, with a condition that works whichever way the truth turns out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא was sitting before רב נחמן and said: Let him bring an animal and bread, and say: 'If the animal that is left is the תמורה, then this new one is the תודה and this is its bread. If the animal that is left is the תודה, then this is its bread and this new animal will be a תמורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new fix is offered for the mixed-up case. Bring a new animal and bread, and state a condition that covers both possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the bread will always belong to whichever animal is the real תודה. If the old animal is the תודה, the new one becomes its תמורה, which needs no bread. That way the new animal is not a 'leftover', so it avoids the problem in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: a substitute animal that someone tried to swap for a קרבן; it becomes holy too
thanks offering, which is brought together with loaves of bread
its bread: the loaves that go with the תודה
this one that is standing, meaning the animal that is still alive

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta was sitting
before Rav Nachman,
and he was sitting and saying:
Let him bring an animal and bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא: אִי הָךְ דְּקָיְימָא תְּמוּרָה הִיא –
phrases.english: and let him say: If this one that is standing is the substitute,
then this is the thanks offering and this is its bread;
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is the new animal he just brought.

phrases.english: and if this one that is standing is the thanks offering,
then this is its bread, and this one will be a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different fix that avoids the 'leftover' problem raised in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: a new animal plus bread with a double condition, so the new animal is either the תודה or a תמורה, never a leftover.

steps.title: רב נחמן: making a תמורה earns forty lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the plan, because it involves making a תמורה on purpose, and that is a sin punished with lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Answer me, my master! Someone who makes a תמורה gets forty lashes on his shoulders, and you call this an allowed plan?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן knocks down the fix from step 2. Under that plan, the new animal might become a תמורה, and making a תמורה is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids swapping an animal for a קרבן, and the punishment is מלקות. A fix cannot be built on planning to do something forbidden, even if it only happens under one side of the condition. So the case is back to having no fix.

keyTerms.meaning: answer me, my master: a polite but sharp way to push back
forty, meaning the forty lashes of מלקות
fit / allowed

phrases.english: He said to him: Answer me, my master,
forty lashes on his shoulders, and it is fit?!
phrases.notes: The one who makes a תמורה gets lashes, so how can it be the plan from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲנִי מָרִי, אַרְבְּעִין בְּכַתְפֵּיהּ, וְכָשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proposal of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole double-condition plan of רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plan calls for making a תמורה on purpose, which is a sin punished with lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: You can't solve a doubt in קדשים by planning to do something forbidden, like making a תמורה.

steps.title: אביי's group suggests bread outside the courtyard wall, based on רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: While visiting the sick רב עילא, אביי and the רבנן suggest a fix: put the bread outside the courtyard wall, with a condition that it is either the תודה's bread or ordinary bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עילא became sick. אביי and the רבנן went to visit him, and they sat and said: If we hold like רבי יוחנן, who said bread outside the courtyard wall still becomes holy, then let the owner bring bread and put it outside the courtyard wall, and say: 'If the animal that is left is the תודה, this is its bread. If not, let the bread go out as חולין.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new fix is offered, this time without any second animal. Only bread is brought, and it is kept outside the courtyard wall with a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that the bread becomes holy at the שחיטה of the תודה even when it is outside the courtyard wall. So bread placed there can work for the תודה if needed. If the animal turns out to be the תמורה, the bread simply stays ordinary, so there is no leftover and no תמורה problem.

keyTerms.meaning: became weak / sick
the wall of the Temple courtyard
becomes holy
ordinary, non-holy food
if it holds / if we accept (a certain view)

phrases.english: Rav Ila became sick,
Abaye and the Rabbis went in to him,
and they were sitting and saying:
If we hold like Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
outside the wall of the courtyard it becomes holy,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the תודה bread: even outside the courtyard wall, it becomes holy when the תודה is slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: לַיְיתֵי לֶחֶם וְלוֹתְבַהּ חוּץ לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: then let him bring bread and place it outside the wall of the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא: אִי הָךְ דְּקָיְימָא תּוֹדָה הִיא –
phrases.english: and let him say: If this one that is standing is the thanks offering,
this is its bread,
and if not, let it go out as ordinary food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב עִילָּא חֲלַשׁ, עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the animal-based fixes failed, this offers a fix that uses only bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: according to רבי יוחנן, bread set outside the courtyard wall with a condition becomes the תודה's bread if needed, and otherwise stays חולין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fix avoids both earlier problems, a planned leftover and a planned תמורה, because no second animal is involved. It only works if רבי יוחנן's view about bread outside the wall is accepted.

steps.title: The bread-outside-the-wall plan fails because of the waving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the fix from אביי and the רבנן: four loaves must be waved "before ה׳", which is only inside the עזרה, but bringing possibly ordinary bread into the עזרה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because four loaves have to be waved, how would he do it? Wave them outside? The פסוק says "before ה׳"! Wave them inside? Then he brings ordinary food into the עזרה! So the plan cannot work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the last plan (keeping the bread outside the wall with a condition) does not work. The problem is the four loaves that have to be waved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four of the תודה's loaves must be waved, and waving only counts inside the עזרה. But according to the condition, the bread might be plain חולין, and you may not bring חולין into the עזרה. Either way he breaks a rule, so the plan fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving: lifting and moving parts of an offering as part of the service
"Before ה׳": a phrase meaning inside the Temple area
Ordinary (not holy) food brought into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
The Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Because there are four to wave,
phrases.notes: He means four loaves out of the forty. These are taken off for the כהן and waved.

phrases.english: how should he do it?
Should he wave them outside?
"Before the Lord" is written!
Inside? Then he is bringing non-holy food into the courtyard!
Therefore, it is not possible.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole plan of putting the bread outside the wall with a condition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The four waved loaves can't be waved outside, and bringing them inside means bringing possible חולין into the עזרה
steps.whatToRemember: Waving must happen inside the עזרה, and possibly-ordinary bread may not go inside. So any plan that leaves the bread's status in doubt runs into this problem.

steps.title: רב שישא's plan: bring eighty loaves using חזקיה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says: according to חזקיה, forty out of eighty loaves become holy. So bring a new animal with eighty loaves and set a condition that works either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא challenged this: If חזקיה is right that forty out of eighty become holy, let him bring an animal with eighty loaves and say: If the animal I still have is the תודה, this new one is also a תודה and the eighty loaves are for both. If the animal I still have is the תמורה, this new one is the תודה, these are its loaves, and forty of the eighty become holy for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא pushes back against "it is not possible" and offers a new plan. He builds it on חזקיה's rule about extra loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה holds that if a תודה is brought with eighty loaves, forty become holy and the rest stay ordinary. So eighty loaves cover both possibilities. If there are two real תודות, all eighty are needed. If only the new one is real, forty become holy for it automatically. No bread has to stay outside, so the waving problem is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it: pushes back on what was just said
Forty out of eighty become holy: חזקיה's rule when a תודה is brought with double the bread
A substitute animal: one that someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which then becomes holy too
Its bread: the loaves that go with a תודה

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi challenged this:
If the view of Chizkiyah is accepted,
who said forty out of eighty become holy,
phrases.notes: This is about a תודה that was slaughtered with eighty loaves instead of the forty it needs.

phrases.english: let him bring an animal,
and bring eighty loaves with it,
and say:
If the one that is still here is the thanks offering,
phrases.notes: "The one still here" means the animal left over after the other one in the mix-up died.

phrases.english: this new one should also be a thanks offering,
and these eighty are for both of them;
if the one that is still here is the substitute,
this new one is the thanks offering and these are its bread,
and let forty out of the eighty become holy for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 5 that no fix is possible, by offering a new plan
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion "לא אפשר" (no fix is possible)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using חזקיה's rule, eighty loaves cover both possibilities without any bread staying outside, so a fix does exist

steps.title: Rejected: holy bread would end up uneaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב שישא's plan because it reduces the eating of the extra forty loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, because he would be cutting down the eating of the forty loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב שישא's plan in one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With eighty loaves, nobody knows which forty are holy. The four loaves taken from the extra forty might be ordinary bread, so the כהנים may not eat them. They might also be the כהן's holy portion, so the owner may not eat them either. That means holy food could go to waste, and causing this is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Reducing the eating: causing holy food to go uneaten and wasted

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the plan fails to make a valid תודה. The problem is that it causes holy bread to be wasted.

phrases.english: Because he reduces the eating of the forty.
phrases.notes: He means the extra forty loaves. Because their status is in doubt, some of them may end up with nobody allowed to eat them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שישא's plan from step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The eighty-loaves plan based on חזקיה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The doubtful loaves can't be eaten by anyone, so holy food is wasted

steps.title: רב אשי's plan: use a pregnant animal, following רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells רב כהנא: according to רבי יוחנן, a pregnant animal and its baby can both serve as one offering. So bring a pregnant animal, wait for the birth, and bring eighty loaves with a condition that works either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: If רבי יוחנן is right that when someone sets aside a pregnant animal as a חטאת and it gives birth, he can get atonement with either the mother or the baby, then let him bring a pregnant animal, wait until it gives birth, and bring eighty loaves. He should say: If the animal I still have is the תמורה, the mother and her baby are thanks offerings and the eighty loaves are for both. If the animal I still have is the תודה, the mother is also a תודה, the eighty loaves are for both, and the baby is the leftover of the תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another plan to get around the problem. The next step gives רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule shows that a mother and her baby can count as one offering, with one of them acting as a spare. Here, every one of the eighty loaves always has a real תודה to go with. If the old animal is the תמורה, the mother and baby are two תודות, each with forty loaves. If the old animal is the real תודה, the old one and the mother are two תודות with the eighty loaves, and the baby is a "leftover" that needs no bread. That may also avoid the problem from step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant animal set aside as a sin offering
Gets atonement through the offering
The baby of an animal
Leftover of a תודה: an extra animal from a תודה that is brought without its own bread

steps.whyThisMatters: This plan tries to answer step 1: here the extra animal is not set aside as a leftover on purpose, because the baby comes along naturally with its mother.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
If the view of Rabbi Yochanan is accepted, who said:
If one set aside a pregnant animal as a sin offering and it gave birth,
if he wants, he gets atonement with the mother;
if he wants, he gets atonement with her baby;
then let him bring a pregnant animal
and wait until it gives birth,
and bring eighty loaves with it, and say:
If the one that is still here is the substitute,
this mother and her baby are thanks offerings,
and these eighty are for both of them;
and if the one that is still here is the thanks offering,
this mother is also a thanks offering,
and these eighty are for both of them,
phrases.notes: "Both" here means the old animal and the new mother.

phrases.english: and this one should be the leftover of the thanks offering.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the baby. A leftover of a תודה is brought without its own bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא אִם אִיתָא לִדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב שישא's plan was rejected, רב אשי offers a different plan that avoids wasting holy bread
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no fix is possible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a pregnant animal, all eighty loaves always belong to a real תודה, and the baby can be the leftover without having been set aside as one on purpose

steps.title: רב כהנא rejects the pregnant-animal plan
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers רב אשי: we cannot be sure that רבי יוחנן lets the owner set aside the baby for its own purpose. Maybe רבי יוחנן's reason is different: a person gets atonement through the natural growth of a holy animal (שבח הקדש).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who says that רבי יוחנן holds that if the owner sets the baby aside, it really is set aside? Maybe he holds that even if the owner sets it aside, it is not set aside. And רבי יוחנן's reason is that he said: A person can get atonement through the growth of a holy animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא pushes back on רב אשי's plan from Step 8. He says the plan is built on a reading of רבי יוחנן that may be wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's plan needed the owner to be able to decide what the baby animal is used for. רב כהנא says maybe רבי יוחנן does not let the owner do that. Maybe the baby just counts as part of the mother because it is 'growth' of something holy. If so, the owner's condition about the baby does nothing, and the plan falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If he set it aside (held it back), it is set aside: the owner's choice about the baby counts
It is not set aside: the owner's choice about the baby does not count
Growth or added value of something holy, like a baby born from a holy animal
Gets atonement through a קרבן
Maybe, perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not saying the baby can't be used for atonement. He agrees רבי יוחנן says it can. He is only arguing about the REASON, and that reason means the owner cannot steer the baby with a condition.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who will tell us
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא answering רב אשי from the step before.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said
if he set it aside, it is set aside?
Perhaps if he set it aside, it is not set aside,
and this is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan,
for he said: A person gets atonement through the growth of something holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's pregnant-animal plan from Step 8 by reading רבי יוחנן differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole pregnant-animal fix proposed by רב אשי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plan assumes the owner can direct the baby with a condition, but רבי יוחנן's rule may come only from שבח הקדש, where the owner's condition does not count.

steps.title: רב דימי suggests a three-animal plan
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי from דמהוריא suggests a new fix: vow a new תודה, bring it plus another animal with eighty loaves, and set a condition so that in every case there are exactly two תודות with eighty loaves, and any extra animal is just a backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came to דמהוריא. רב דימי son of רב הונא from דמהוריא said to רבינא: Let him bring an animal and say 'It is upon me' (a new vow). Then let him bring another animal, bring eighty loaves with it, and say: If the animal that is left is the תמורה, then these two new animals are תודות and the eighty loaves are for both of them. And if the animal that is left is the תודה, then the one I vowed with 'upon me' is also a תודה, the eighty loaves are for the two of them, and the other new animal is a backup.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rabbi offers yet another way to save the mixed-up animals. He uses a fresh vow and an extra animal so the numbers work out no matter which animal is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was: the animal left over is either the תודה (needs forty loaves) or the תמורה (needs no loaves). With this plan there are always exactly two real תודות, so eighty loaves (forty each) always fit. If the leftover is the תמורה, the two new animals are the two תודות; if the leftover is the תודה, it pairs with the vowed one, and the third animal is only a backup, which needs no loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal; it becomes holy too, but a תודה's תמורה does not get loaves
'It is upon me': the wording of a vow that makes you obligated to bring a קרבן
Backup, a guarantee: an animal ready in case the main קרבן gets lost
Happened to come to a place
The one that is still standing, the one that's left

phrases.english: Ravina happened to come to Dimhorya,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב דִּימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Dimi, son of Rav Huna,
from Dimhorya, said to Ravina:
Let him bring an animal and say: 'It is upon me,'
phrases.notes: He means a brand-new vow to bring a תודה, and this animal pays off that vow.

phrases.english: and let him bring another animal,
and let him bring eighty loaves with it and say:
If this one that is left is the substitute,
these two are thanks offerings,
phrases.notes: 'These two' are the two new animals he just brought.

phrases.english: and these eighty are for both of them;
and if this one that is left is the thanks offering,
then this one about which I said 'upon me' should also be a thanks offering,
and these eighty are for the two of them,
and the other one should be a backup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי's plan was rejected, a new rabbi offers a different fix to the same problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (רבי חייא's view) that there is no fix when a תודה and its תמורה got mixed up and one died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By making a new vow and adding a backup animal, the owner can make sure there are always exactly two תודות matching eighty loaves, whichever animal is left.

steps.title: רבינא rejects the plan: don't make vows on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the plan is no good because it requires making a new vow on purpose, and the פסוק says it is better not to vow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Torah said, 'It is better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.' And you are saying: Let him get up and make a vow from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shoots down רב דימי's plan. The plan only works if the person makes a fresh vow, and we don't tell people to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan from Step 10 starts with saying 'הרי עלי', a new vow. רבינא points to a פסוק that says not vowing is better than vowing. So a fix that depends on telling someone to vow is not acceptable, even if the math works.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a vow (נדר)
From the start, on purpose, before anything has happened
Let him get up (and do it), meaning: go ahead deliberately

steps.whatToRemember: Every fix in this sugya was rejected: the backup animal set aside as a leftover, רבי יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא's animal-plus-bread plan, the bread outside the wall, רב שישא's eighty loaves, רב אשי's pregnant animal, and רב דימי's three animals. So רבי חייא's statement stands: once a תודה and its תמורה are mixed and one dies, there is no fix.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a halachic fix must not only work on paper; it also cannot ask a person to do something the Torah discourages, like making a new vow.

phrases.english: He said to him: The Torah said:
'It is better that you do not vow
than that you vow and do not pay,'
and you say: Let him get up and vow from the start?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה טוֹב אֲשֶׁר לֹא תִדֹּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's three-animal plan from Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire three-animal plan, since it starts with a new vow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plan requires making a fresh vow on purpose, which the פסוק in קהלת discourages.

steps.title: New משנה: a vowed thanks offering comes from ordinary money
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: someone who says 'הרי עלי תודה' must bring the animal and its loaves from חולין, ordinary non-holy money.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who says, 'It is upon me to bring a תודה,' must bring it and its loaves from ordinary (non-holy) money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is over, and a new משנה starts a new topic. It tells us what money must be used to pay for a vowed תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'הרי עלי' makes the תודה a real obligation, a debt. Because of that, both the animal and its loaves must be paid for with חולין money, not money that is already holy for another reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of the משנה text
From ordinary, non-holy money or property
Its bread: the loaves that come with a תודה

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says, 'It is upon me to bring a thanks offering,'
must bring it and its loaves from non-holy money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ended with every fix rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who vows 'הרי עלי תודה' must bring the animal and its loaves from חולין.
